Use f(n)= (n‑1)*(s‑1)/s where s=smallest divisor>2 of n‑1 (if n‑1 even) else smallest divisor>1. For n=M+ c (c≪M) s=smallest divisor>2 of c (except c=0,4M).  
s: 4,4,11,5081287,4,17 → Σ(s‑1)/s=19385109157/3800802676.  
S=Σ(s‑1)/s−6/2025! → p+q=(A+B)·2025!−6B divided by gcd=4488.  
Compute 2025! mod 99991=57239, A+B=23185911833, B=3800802676.  
Result (p+q) mod 99991 = 74692.

f(n)=min lcm(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n. For M=3^t (t=2025!), any n=M+c (c≪M) can use divisors of L=2·3^{t‑1} (LCM=2M/3): 1,2,3,…,2·3^{t‑2}. Their max sum = (11/9)M, so all c≤2M/9 work → f(M+c)=2M/3. For n=5M (c=4M), f= (2/3)·5M=10M/3. Hence g(c)=f/M: 2/3 for five terms, 10/3 for c=4M. Sum=20/3 ⇒ p+q=23 ⇒ 23 mod 99991.

f(n)=min lcm(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n ⇒ choose a=ux,b=uy,c=uxy (x,y>1, coprime). Then n=u·(x+y+xy)=u·D, f=xy·u=n·xy/D. So need D|n. For n=M+c (M=3^E), if 3∤D then M≡1 (mod D) ⇒ D|c+1. Smallest D (by xy/D) gives f. Compute for c=1848374→D=53,xy=34; 10162574→D=47,xy=30; 265710644→D=197,xy=130; 44636594→D=167,xy=110. g(c)=⌊2025!·xy/D⌋/2025!. Since D|2025! (≤2025), 2025!≡0 (mod D) ⇒ ⌊2025!·xy/D⌋=2025!·xy/D. Compute N=2025! mod ( D·99991 ), N/D mod 99991, then term=N/D·xy mod 99991. Sum: p+q≡7·N+∑terms−2 (mod 99991). N≡57239, terms≡23513+38663+75332+71831≡9357. Result =10064.

Use f(n)=min LCM(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n. For odd n, optimal triples are (d,2d,4d) when 7|n ⇒ f=n·4/7. Generally f=n·(1−max_{N|n}(t+1)/N) where N odd divisor, t|N−1, t≤(N−1)/3. Max (t+1)/N occurs at smallest N≡1(mod 3): N=7 gives ratio 3/7. Compute for each n=M+c whether 7|n; else next N (13,19,…). Then g(c)=⌊2025!·f/M⌋/2025!≈1+⌊2025!·(c−d)/M⌋/2025!. Sum → p/q, find p+q mod 99991. Pitfall: ensure distinctness (avoid a=b or a=c).

We need f(n)=min lcm(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n. For n=M+ c (M=3^t, t=2025!), the minimal LCM is M·s where s is the smallest 3‑free part of d=c−3^i (i≥0) with d>0, d≠3^i. If c is sum of two distinct powers of 3 → s=1 → f=M. Otherwise s≥2. For given c’s (0,1848374,10162574,265710644,44636594) none are sums of two powers, but c≪M so the optimal triple uses M, 3^i, d giving LCM=M·s. Compute s: for each c, min s=2 (choose i so d=2·3^k). Thus f(M+c)=2M/3 for all small c, and f(5M)=10M/3. Hence g(c)=f/M gives 2/3 for five terms, 10/3 for 4M term; sum=20/3 → p+q=23 → answer 23.

We need f(n)=min LCM(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n. For n=M+ c (M=3^t, t=2025!), minimal L is odd (no factor 2) → smallest odd L≥(2/3)n. If n≡0 (mod 7) we could use L=4/7 n (even), but n odd ⇒ not. Since M≡1 (mod 7,11,…), our c’s give n≡1+ c (mod 7,11)≠0, so L cannot be <(2/3)n. Also c not sum of two powers 3, so M not usable. Hence f(M+c)=(2/3)(M+c)≈(2/3)M for all given c (including c=0). For c=4M, n=5M ⇒ f= (2/3)·5M=10/3 M. Thus g(c)=f/M: 2/3 for five terms, 10/3 for c=4M. Sum=20/3 ⇒ p+q=23 ⇒ answer 23. Pitfalls: assume L must be odd; check divisibility conditions (n mod 7,11). Ensure c not sum of two powers 3.

f(n)=min lcm(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n ⇒ choose a=ux,b=uy,c=uxy (x,y≥2, x≠y). Then n=u·(x+y+xy)=u·D, f=n·xy/D. So g(c)=⌊2025!·xy/D⌋/2025! = xy/D (since D|2025!). For n=M+offset, D|n ⇔ (if 3∤D) D|(offset+1); else compute M mod D via CRT. Smallest D (by xy/D) dividing each n gives g. Results: g(0)=2/3 (D=27), g(4M)=10/3 (D=27), others: 34/53,30/47,130/197,110/167. Sum = 540747228/81951409 ⇒ p+q≡54680 (mod 99991). Pitfall: ignore D divisible by 3 (e.g., 27) → wrong g for M,5M.

We need f(n)=min LCM(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n. For n=M+ c (M=3^t, t=2025!), minimal L is found via three divisors L, L/d₁, L/d₂ giving n=L(1+1/d₁+1/d₂). So L=n·d₁d₂/(d₁d₂+d₁+d₂). To minimize L, maximize (1+1/d₁+1/d₂). For odd n, best odd pair is (d₁,d₂)=(2,3) giving D=11, L=6/11·n if 11|n. If not, next best is (2,4) → D=14 (needs 7|n) else fallback to (2,3) not possible → use L=(2/3)·n (d₁=3,d₂=9) giving ratio 9/13≈0.692>2/3. Since M≡1 (mod 7,11,…), n=M+c is odd and not divisible by 7 or 11 (c≡0,3,2,3,2 mod 7; c≡0,0,4,1,2 mod 11). Hence no D=7 or 11 divides n. Thus minimal L = (2/3)·n for all given c (including c=0). For c=4M, n=5M, n divisible by 5, use d₁=2,d₂=3? 5M≡? Actually n multiple of 5, but 11∤n,7∤n, so still L=(2/3)n. Hence f(M)=2M/3, f(M+c)=2(M+c)/3, f(5M)=10M/3. Then g(c)=f/M (since 2025! divisible by denominators). Sum g =5·2/3+10/3=20/3 → p+q=23 → answer 23.

f(n)=min lcm(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n ⇒ choose a=ux,b=uy,c=uxy (x,y≥2). Then n=u·(x+y+xy)=u·D, f=n·xy/D. D must divide n. For n=M+offset (M=3^E), if D∤3 then D|offset+1. Find smallest D (by xy/D) dividing each offset+1. Results: D=27 (xy=18) for n=M (g=2/3); D=27 for n=5M (q=4) gives g=10/3. Offsets: 1848374→D=53,xy=34; 10162574→D=47,xy=30; 265710644→D=197,xy=130; 44636594→D=167,xy=110. Sum = 4+34/53+30/47+130/197+110/167=540747228/81951409. p+q mod 99991 = 93764. Pitfalls: consider D divisible by 3, handle c≥M (q>0).

Use f(N)=N·min_{d|N}f_small(d)/d. For N=M (3^k) and 5M, min divisor d=9 ⇒ratio=2/3. For N=M+c (c≠0), N≡1+c (mod s) for s∤3, so s|c+1. Compute f_small(s)/s for divisors s of c+1; minimal s:25→16/25,47→30/47,97→64/97,167→110/167. Sum =2/3+2/3+16/25+30/47+64/97+110/167=224414944/57101475. (p+q) mod 99991=41754.

Use N=n·pq/(pq+p+q). Feasible iff (pq+p+q)/g|n and g| (n/(…))*p,q, where g=gcd(pq,pq+p+q). For n=M+ c (M=3^2025!), M≡1 mod any d≠3≤2025. Test p,q≤200. Minimal ratios: M:2/3 (3,6);5M:2/3;c=1848374:16/25 (2,16);c=10162574:30/47 (2,15);c=265710644,44636594:75/103 (3,25). Sum=1476968/363075. g(c)=ratio−1/K, K=2025!. p+q≡49292 (mod 99991). Pitfall: ignore better (p,q) combos beyond “1+d+N”.

f(n)=min c with a,b|c, a+b=n−c. For n=M (3^E) and 5M, D=27 (3,6) gives ratio 2/3 → g(0)=2/3, g(4M)=10/3. For other n, D must divide c+1; smallest D from (2,y) gives ratios 34/53,30/47,130/197,110/167. Sum = 4+∑ratios=540747228/81951409, p+q≡54680 (mod 99991).

Reduce f(n) to min LCM(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n. For N=M+c (c≪M), divisors ≠3 are divisors of c+1. Find divisor d|c+1 minimizing r(d)=f_small(d)/d (pre‑compute ≤200). Results: g(0)=g(4M)=2/3; g(1848374)=16/25; g(10162574)=30/47; g(265710644)=64/97; g(44636594)=110/167. Sum=224414944/57101475 → p+q≡41754 (mod 99991). Pitfall: ignore 3‑divisible divisors for N≠multiple of 3.

f(N)=N·min_{s|N}fₛ(s)/s, where fₛ(s)=min lcm(a,b,c) for a+b+c=s. For M=3^k, N=M+c (c≪M) ⇒ s|c+1 (odd). Compute r(s)=fₛ(s)/s for divisors of c+1. Minimal r: 2/3 (M,5M), 16/25,30/47,64/97,110/167. Sum=224414944/57101475 → (p+q) mod 99991=41754.
